verdict.rationale: Pandoc's own documentation covers converting between rich formats such as docx, HTML, LaTeX and PDF, and lets users style output through templates and --css. Community reports confirm it keeps semantic structure: headers map to real Word styles, tables carry correct data into Word reports, and a novel's PDF output was clean enough for a publisher to use. However, several users report fidelity loss. One says documents were 'butchered' because the internal representation was less expressive than the formats. Others report tables breaking with overlapping text or misaligned cells, tables in docx not autofitting, and Unicode characters silently dropped in PDF. Layout and fonts come from user-supplied templates and reference docs rather than being carried over from the source. Missing for 10: documented preservation of source layout and fonts, evidenced image-fidelity handling, and reliable table layout in PDF/docx output.
